purpose: Compile already-owned Supreme operating discipline into enforceable evidence gates so configured execution cannot silently skip verification-before-completion.

submission_gates.evidence: Exact Supreme manifest/configuration revision recorded before task work.
Runtime, repository/environment snapshot, allowed dependencies/tools, and task artifacts inspected before implementation.
Requested behavior, preserved behavior, explicit invariants, and forbidden changes enumerated from task bytes before coding.
Task risk classified and verification depth selected. Security, concurrency, persistence, performance, parsing, and recovery tasks require adversarial/boundary verification.
For repair tasks, causal failure reproduced before change when possible. For greenfield tasks, a concrete threat/boundary model or failing local check exists before completion.
Changes stay inside the smallest sufficient causal surface and preserve explicit invariants.
Candidate passes task-relevant independent checks that do not depend on benchmark solution/verifier logic. Public standards/corpora/fuzz/property checks should be reused when available.
At least one adversarial/boundary test class beyond happy-path checks is executed and preserved.
Every acceptance criterion and invariant is mapped to observed evidence; unresolved known gaps block submission.
No solution/task-specific verifier logic was read before submission; spent tasks cannot be recycled as fresh promotion evidence.

generic_regression_from_first_preflight.lesson: Textual configuration ownership is insufficient if execution can bypass its mandatory verification discipline.
